trust_decision.summary: Whether a template name may cause the Spring loader to open a resource outside the configured prefix and without the configured suffix: decided by rejecting protocol-lifted, fragment/query and traversal locations in SpringTemplateLoader.resolve/getResource, and by rejecting such Spring MVC view names in HandlebarsViewResolver.configure.

landing_point.why: The summary names SpringTemplateLoader and its suffix bypass, and the .hbs suffix is appended in resolve() (handlebars-springmvc/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/springmvc/SpringTemplateLoader.java:66-77) and then handed as a plain string to Spring's ResourceLoader at handlebars-springmvc/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/springmvc/SpringTemplateLoader.java:58, which reinterprets '#'/'?' as URL components instead of path characters.

fix_sites.entry_point: HandlebarsViewResolver.buildView(String) reached from ViewResolver.resolveViewName(String, Locale) (Spring MVC view resolution)
fix_sites.module_kind: Spring MVC web layer (view resolver wrapper over Handlebars.compile)

fix_sites.entry_point: SpringTemplateLoader.sourceAt(String) and resolve(String), i.e. the public TemplateLoader API reached from Handlebars.compile(String) and from render-time partial resolution (handlebars/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/internal/Partial.java:201)
fix_sites.module_kind: resource loader (TemplateLoader implementation over Spring ResourceLoader)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names SpringTemplateLoader, and the view resolver is only a web-layer wrapper whose names come from the application's own controllers, so hardening the loader looks like it already closes that route.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The loader must keep accepting protocol-qualified locations ('classpath:page.html', 'file:C:/page.html'); a fix that rejects ':' (or '#'/'..') inside getResource breaks every legitimate classpath: template load, which is the normal Spring configuration and what the fix's own loader tests use as prefix.

O6_input_shapes: protocol-prefixed name: file:/... or classpath:/... lifted in front of the resolved location
name with a '#' so the appended '.hbs' suffix lands in the URL fragment
name with a '?' so the appended suffix lands in the URL query
absolute/leading-slash name, where the leading '/' must be preserved after normalization

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ServletContextTemplateLoader validates only the path prefix inside classpathResource() (handlebars/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/io/URLTemplateLoader.java:75-93) and then hands the name to servletContext.getResource(); the fragment/query component validation the fix adds to SpringTemplateLoader has no counterpart, so a name that moves the '.hbs' suffix into a URL ref is not rejected.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is titled SpringTemplateLoader / Spring MVC, and servlet-context lookups are the container's own resource API where '#' is usually taken literally.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other Maven module (handlebars core) and package com.github.jknack.handlebars.io, two files away from the springmvc landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a shared validateNoUnsafeUrlComponents(URL)-style check applied to every URLTemplateLoader subclass
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same 'the suffix lands in the URL component' problem appears whenever a location string is turned into a URL, so a maintainer hardening SpringTemplateLoader would plausibly put the check in the shared base class the other loaders already use.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the servlet analogue of the Spring loader, hardened the same way (reject refs/queries on the URL the container returns)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the only other loader in the family that yields container-built URLs, and it is configured exactly like the Spring one (prefix, suffix, webapp-relative).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a resolver variant that wires a ServletContextTemplateLoader (or any non-Spring loader) instead of SpringTemplateLoader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: createTemplateLoader already chooses the loader by configuration, and the constructor at handlebars-springmvc/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/springmvc/HandlebarsViewResolver.java:143-148 shows externally supplied Handlebars instances are a supported deployment.

O9_family: path traversal / arbitrary file read (CWE-22, CWE-23, CWE-552)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module (no mvnw wrapper), JDK 17 (maven.compiler.release=17 at pom.xml:505), Spring 6.2.9, JUnit 5 + Mockito for module tests
O10_build.project_tests: handlebars-springmvc: SpringTemplateLoaderTest (two tests at the pin: sourceAt reading src/test/resources/template.hbs, and fileNotFound), HandlebarsViewTest, MessageSourceHelperTest, and Spring-context tests Issue257/Issue292/Issue304 driven by HandlebarsApp; core area tests: ClassPathTemplateLoaderTest, FileTemplateLoaderTest, ServletContextTemplateLoaderTest, CompositeTemplateLoaderTest

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject '#' (or any ':'/'#'/'..') in the view name inside HandlebarsViewResolver.configure and stop, leaving SpringTemplateLoader.resolve() to keep lifting a 'file:' protocol in front of the resolved location for direct sourceAt/resolve callers.

out_of_scope_notes: Outside this advisory: I18nHelper.UTF8Control.newBundle loads a .properties classpath resource from a template-supplied bundle basename (handlebars/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/helper/I18nHelper.java:337-352); not pursued.
